messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall for incidents@redwood — critical: Kyte (enterprise VPC) experiencing 30-60% KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse in dedicated pool kyte-prod-1. Auto-alert: latency up, token cost spike. Runbook: /runbooks/kv_cache_prefix_hitrate

oncall-sre: I’m on it. jumping in — checking dashboards now. @alex.m @priya please standby for escalation if this is tenant-isolation.

alex.m: looking at the per-tenant metrics — Kyte shows sudden drop at 2155001000 across all regions attached to kyte-prod-1. other tenants on that pool look fine. suspiciously correlated with a background prefetch job.

priya: confirmed. Sample metric: kyte-prod-1.kv_prefix.hitrate = 0.19 (baseline 0.92). Cache size steady, evictions spiked. logs show repeated prefix insertions from prefetcher: `prefetcher/assign prefix=kyte:session: user=unknown batch=128`

mike-fab: copying relevant log window: ```
2026-03-15T12:03:20Z prefetcher INFO assign_prefix tenant=kyte prefix=kyte:session:abc123 -> backend=shared-kv-42
2026-03-15T12:03:20Z cache INFO insert key=kyte:session:abc123 shard=3
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z prefetcher ERROR missing-tenant-metadata for token=... fallback-assign tenant=kyte -> backend=shared-kv-42
```

eng-lead-ryan: this looks like cache pollution from a mis-scoped prefetch job that used shared backend assignment causing cross-tenant prefix collisions. For Kyte we need tenant-scoped namespace and to evict polluted prefixes ASAP. Potential mitigation: (1) throttle prefetch for kyte, (2) create tenant-scoped cache namespace, (3) flush/evict keys matching kyte:session:* on affected shards, (4) roll cache instances if stateful corruption persists.

cs-kyte: Kyte reporting degraded request latency for user-facing inference calls ~> 800ms and elevated cost. They want ETA on mitigation and whether this will require a maintenance window.

oncall-sre: Messaging Kyte: short notice mitigation to reduce customer impact — we will throttle prefetch and evict polluted prefixes, no downtime expected. ETA ~20-30m. @cs-kyte please relay.

cs-kyte: relayed. They approved immediate mitigation; want a short post-incident note when done.

mike-fab: running targeted eviction dry-run to ensure we don't wipe legitimate keys. Command I will run: ```
# list sample keys matching kyte prefix on shard 3
redis-cli -h shard-3.kv.internal --scan --pattern 'kyte:session:*' --count 100
# then delete only keys with ts < 2026-03-15T12:00:00 by checking key metadata
```

priya: while that runs, we can flip prefetcher to tenant-scoped mode for kyte. patch to prefetcher config: ```diff
- assign_strategy: shared_backend
+ assign_strategy_overrides:
+  kyte: tenant_scoped_backend
```

oncall-sre: approve patch for immediate hotfix. keep it scoped to kyte to avoid global risk. mike, proceed with eviction after dry-run OK. alex, add a temporary rate-limit on prefetcher for kyte (50r/s).

alex.m: applied rate-limit for kyte prefetcher: `prefetch_rate_limit.kyte=50` — watching metrics.

mike-fab: dry-run looks good; keys selected are from failed prefetch attempts and low TTL. proceeding with evict (one shard at a time). Running: ```
redis-cli -h shard-3.kv.internal --scan --pattern 'kyte:session:*' | xargs -r redis-cli -h shard-3.kv.internal del
```

ops-runner-bot: Eviction job started on shard-3 by mike-fab at 2155001605. ETA per shard ~2m.

oncall-sre: after shard-3 eviction, observing kyte hit-rate -> 0.62 (was 0.19). latency down to ~320ms. good sign. continuing with shards 1,2,4.

eng-lead-ryan: while evictions are progressing, schedule an immediate config change to make kyte use tenant-scoped cache namespace permanently for kyte-prod-1. I'll open a canary rollout to 10% traffic to verify no regressions.

priya: prepared canary config snippet: ```yaml
cache_namespace_overrides:
  kyte:
    namespace: kyte_ns_v2
    prefetch_assign: tenant_scoped
```

cs-kyte: Kyte says they see improvement, thanks. They asked whether their tokens were exposed to other tenants — confirm?

oncall-sre: we believe no data leakage of token payloads occurred — pollution was prefix collisions and unnecessary cache entries. We'll confirm after inspecting key metadata and audit logs. Marking as potential isolation breach until confirmed.

mike-fab: audit logs show prefetcher used fallback path due to missing tenant metadata; keys inserted had empty tenant header but prefix still had kyte:. no evidence keys from other tenants were read as kyte data. marking low-risk.

ops-runner-bot: All targeted evictions completed across shards at 2155002550.

oncall-sre: final metrics: kyte.kv_prefix.hitrate = 0.88, latency ~180ms, error rate back to baseline. Cost spike subsiding.

eng-lead-ryan: rolling kyte tenant-scoped config to 10% passed canary; proceed to 100% in 10m. Also adding an automated assertion to the prefetcher: if tenant metadata missing -> skip prefetch and emit metric.

priya: created a short-term alert rule to catch prefix-hit drops for any enterprise VPC tenant: `alert:kvs_prefix_hitrate_drop severity=high scope=tenant` and a runbook link.

cs-kyte: confirmed Kyte is back to normal and appreciates our quick response. They requested a summary and timeline.

oncall-sre: drafting post-incident note. Action items: (1) permanent tenant-scoped namespace for kyte, (2) prefetcher hard-fail on missing tenant metadata, (3) improved canary for cache namespace rollouts, (4) postmortem + share with Kyte. Assign owners: ryan -> config rollout, priya -> prefetcher fix, alex -> alerts and monitoring, mike -> postmortem data collection.

mike-fab: collecting TTL/key-age distribution for postmortem. snippet: ```
redis-cli -h shard-3.kv.internal --scan --pattern 'kyte:session:*' --type string | xargs -I{} redis-cli -h shard-3.kv.internal ttl {}
```

oncall-sre: closing incident thread once postmortem PR is merged. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved: kyte prefix cache pollution mitigated, status: resolved, severity: critical -> mitigated. Postmortem due in 72h.
